summary: Push Notifications backend integration (iteration_3) FULLY VERIFIED. New /api/register-push endpoint + friend_request/friend_accept/friend_at_club notification side-effects + push_service relay wiring all working as specced. 9/9 new push tests PASS, 21/21 prior friends-system regression suite still PASS (30/30 total = 100%). Confirmed via backend logs: upstream relay at integrations.emergentagent.com is actually called and returns 401 (placeholder EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY), and push_service soft-fails (logs 'EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY missing or invalid') without ever propagating an exception — endpoints /api/friends/request, /api/friends/{id}/accept, /api/checkins all return 200 despite upstream rejection. db.push_tokens persistence verified (upsert with device_token + last_register_ok=False). Privacy invariants verified both directions: (a) when sender visibility=hidden, NO friend_at_club notification is created for friends; (b) when friend visibility=hidden, that friend receives NO friend_at_club notification. /api/register-push correctly returns 403 on user_id mismatch and 401/403 when unauthenticated. No regressions; no critical issues. Frontend testing intentionally skipped per request (push tokens require a real device — Expo web returns null).

minor.issue: The friend_at_club push block is wrapped in a single broad try/except that also swallows any notifications.insert_many error. Push is correctly best-effort, but a DB insert failure on the in-app notifications collection would now be silently logged — consider splitting the try/except so DB errors surface while only the upstream push call is best-effort. Not blocking; current behavior matches spec ('endpoint must return 200 even when push fails').

db.notifications.insert_one is NOT inside try/except (only push_service.send_push is). If MongoDB is unavailable for the notifications collection, the friend request/accept would 500. Same pattern as before push was added — flagging for awareness, not a regression.

action_items: (Optional/cosmetic) In /api/checkins, split the friend_at_club try/except so DB errors on db.notifications.insert_many are not silently swallowed; only push_service.send_push needs to be best-effort.

(Optional) Consider rate-limiting /api/register-push to avoid token spam from a malicious client (currently no rate limit, upserts unbounded per user/platform — fine in practice since platform is the unique key).

(Carry-over from iteration_2) Replace deprecated 'shadow*' RN style props with 'boxShadow'; replace pointerEvents prop with style.pointerEvents; guard expo-notifications listeners with Platform.OS !== 'web' — these are FE-only and not in scope for this iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: push_service.py is well-designed: never raises, soft-fails on 401 (placeholder key) and >=400, caps recipients to 100, supports idempotency_key. Good defensive code.

server.py grew from 1700 → 1906 lines; the new /register-push + push side-effects are tightly coupled into existing routes. With friends/notifications/push surfaces, splitting server.py into routers/ (push.py, friends.py, notifications.py, checkins.py) is now overdue.

Privacy filter in /api/checkins is correctly applied in TWO directions before sending push (sender visibility check + recipient visibility filter via $ne='hidden' Mongo query). Verified by integration tests.
Idempotency keys are well-chosen: fr_req_{fs_id}, fr_acc_{friendship_id}, ci_{checkin_id} — prevents duplicate push deliveries on client retries.
register_device + send_push share a module-level singleton httpx.AsyncClient with a default 10s timeout; the aclose() hook is correctly wired into FastAPI shutdown.

rca_of_issue: No bugs found. All push integration points behave per spec. Verified upstream relay actually receives requests (backend logs show 'EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY missing or invalid (register)' and '(trigger)' warnings on every call), confirming the httpx call path is exercised end-to-end and the soft-failure handling correctly converts 401 → return False without raising.
